_comment: Ground truth for the simulated enterprise systems. This is the world the
tools observe -- it is NOT the workflow's answer key. The graph never reads
this file: it has to reach the root cause through search_logs /
get_service_metrics / search_knowledge_base / get_incident_history like a
real engineer would. Handout ground rule 16 bans hard-coding the visible
answers into the workflow; giving the mock systems a consistent internal
state is what makes the simulation honest rather than what makes it cheat.
Six services, six deliberately different resolution paths:
payment-service   two steps, low-risk then high-risk -- both sides of the
approval fork inside one incident, plus a flaky metrics
backend on the first call (FR15).
identity-service  one high-risk action that must be aimed at the right
change_id; the wrong id executes and changes nothing.
order-service     one action that auto-executes with no approver, because
the service is low impact. Symptoms deliberately
resemble payment-service; the correct action differs.
catalog-service   one low-risk pool resize fully resolves the incident;
the running process reloads the new ceiling.
inventory-service scaling only partially helps; an approved restart is
required to reclaim leaked connections.
reporting-service nothing available fixes it. Exists so the replan loop
has to give up and escalate (FR13/FR14) rather than
always finding a happy ending.
To add the hidden scenario: append one entry under 'services'. No code change.

knowledge_base.title: Database connection pool exhaustion under load
symptoms: request timed out waiting for connection
error rate spike with normal CPU
knowledge_base.probable_cause: All pooled connections are checked out and callers queue until they time out. The ceiling is too low for current traffic; connections are being returned normally, there are just not enough of them.
knowledge_base.content: Raise the pool ceiling first, then restart so the running process picks it up. A restart on its own frees the pool for about a minute before it saturates again. Distinguish from a leak: under saturation, connection hold times stay short and traffic is elevated.

knowledge_base.title: Token validation failures after signing key rotation
symptoms: token rejected unable to verify signature
login failures with normal identity provider latency
knowledge_base.probable_cause: A key rotation retired a signing key that is still present in tokens issued before the rotation, so the validator can no longer resolve the kid.
knowledge_base.content: Roll the JWKS configuration back so the retired key is served again until every in-flight token has expired. Restarting the service does not restore a key that was removed from the key set. Find the change id in the service's own configuration log lines before rolling anything back.

knowledge_base.title: Connection leak introduced by a deployment
symptoms: connections checked out for long periods
response time increased with normal cpu and normal traffic
knowledge_base.probable_cause: A code path acquires connections and never returns them, so free capacity drains over time even though request volume is unchanged. The pool ceiling is not the problem.
knowledge_base.content: A restart reclaims every leaked connection immediately and is the fastest route back to service. Raising the ceiling only buys time -- the leak drains the larger pool too. Rolling back the offending deploy stops new leaking but does not reclaim connections already held by running processes.

knowledge_base.title: Service restart runbook
knowledge_base.probable_cause: Process-level state that cannot be cleared while the service is running.
knowledge_base.content: A rolling restart drops in-flight requests. On a business-critical service it is treated as high risk and needs an approver; on a low-impact service it is routine and executes without one.

knowledge_base.title: Rolling back a configuration or deployment change
symptoms: incident started shortly after a change
knowledge_base.probable_cause: A recent change introduced the fault.
knowledge_base.content: Correlate the incident start time with the change before rolling back, and pass the change id that actually caused it -- reverting an unrelated change executes successfully and fixes nothing. Rollback is always high risk: it reverts everything else that shipped in the same change.

knowledge_base.title: Infrastructure saturation
knowledge_base.probable_cause: The host or container is out of headroom.
knowledge_base.content: Confirm CPU and memory are genuinely saturated before acting. Normal CPU during a latency incident rules this out and points somewhere else.

knowledge_base.title: Upstream dependency degradation
symptoms: upstream latency elevated while local resources are normal
knowledge_base.probable_cause: The fault is in a system this platform does not operate. Local metrics other than queue depth and latency stay at baseline.
knowledge_base.content: There is no local action that resolves this. Restarting or resizing the dependent service does not change an upstream fault and costs availability for nothing. Record the evidence, stop attempting remediation, and escalate to the owning team.

incident_history.summary: Payment error rate rose to 12% with database connection timeouts.
incident_history.root_cause: Connection pool exhausted after a traffic increase; ceiling was sized for 2024 volumes.
incident_history.resolution_action: Pool size raised from 20 to 50, followed by a restart to apply it.

incident_history.summary: Intermittent authorisation failures from the upstream provider.
incident_history.resolution_action: Waited for the provider; no local action taken.

incident_history.summary: Widespread login failures; tokens rejected at validation.
incident_history.root_cause: Expired signing certificate was still referenced by the JWKS endpoint.
incident_history.resolution_action: Configuration rolled back, then the certificate was replaced during a maintenance window.

incident_history.summary: Order lookups slowed to several seconds two hours after a release.
incident_history.root_cause: A connection leak on the order-history path; connections were acquired and never returned.
incident_history.resolution_action: Rolling restart reclaimed the leaked connections; the leak was patched in the next release.

incident_history.summary: Checkout errors during a regional network partition.
incident_history.root_cause: Packet loss between the application and database subnets.
incident_history.resolution_action: Network team rerouted; no application change.

incident_history.summary: Scheduled reports failed to generate for four hours.
incident_history.root_cause: The upstream analytics warehouse was in a degraded state during a vendor migration.
incident_history.resolution_action: Escalated to the data platform team; no local remediation was possible or attempted.
